Subject: Lead Escrow & Revenue Waterfall for Beacon Integrations

Hi Priya / Beacon team,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As we discussed, Redwood is excited to pursue a structured go-to-market for Beacon integrations that protects lead ownership while keeping commercial ops simple. To move from concept to contracting quickly, we put together two items for your review:

- Draft MoU that outlines referral/resale paths and a simple lead escrow mechanism (attached: Beacon_MoU_draft_v2.pdf).
- A proposed commission waterfall (high-level) for referral -> implementation -> renewal events. We can follow with a spreadsheet that models monthly payouts.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Beacon confirm the team that will own lead registration (name/email) and the acceptance criteria (e.g., verified demo, qualified account)?
- Are there procurement or legal constraints (standard PO terms, required insurance, guaranteed SLAs) we should be aware of early?
- Preference check: would Beacon prefer referral credits that convert to reseller margin or direct rev-share on invoiced ARR?

If it helps, Ben (cc'd on follow-ups) can share the waterfall workbook so we can align on percentages and thresholds. Suggest a 30-minute sync this week to walk items and agree next steps.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Best,

Hi Priya / team — attaching a simple waterfall workbook (commission_waterfall.xlsx) to make the options concrete. High-level summary:

- Referral path: 8% of first-year net ARR credited to Beacon as a one-time payment after invoice (no ongoing margin).
- Resale path: 18% gross margin on first year, then 10% on renewal where Beacon remains active reseller. Revenue recognized monthly based on collections.
- Implementation uplift: fixed partner implementation fee split 60/40 (Beacon/Redwood) when Beacon provides professional services.
- Registration window: default 90 days from initial registration; enterprise exceptions to be agreed case-by-case.

Notes and assumptions are on the first tab of the spreadsheet. Key operational asks:
- Lead registration form: name, company, contact email, demo date, expected ARR band.
- Escrow custody: we propose a simple shared Google Sheet + HubSpot tag + locked archived confirmation email as the canonical registration record. If Beacon needs a third-party escrow account (legal custody), we can add that to the MoU but it will increase operational overhead.

Happy to walk through the workbook on Friday. Suggested attendees: Priya, Procurement (if they want), Camila (partner ops), Evelyn (partnership lead), and me.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood-inference.com

Subject: Re: Lead Escrow & Revenue Waterfall for Beacon Integrations — Legal/ops notes

Folks — quick set of redlines/operational notes from partner ops / legal perspective:

1) Escrow mechanism: prefer minimal friction — maintain HubSpot lead record + timestamped confirmation email as source-of-truth. If Beacon insists on a third-party escrow (fund or custodian), we should table the change to avoid delaying commercial terms.

2) Registration window: propose 90 days standard with a clause that enterprise-level opportunities (>$250k ARR) convert to 12-month protection once a joint qualification call occurs. This avoids disputes for larger deals while keeping small leads from locking up accounts.

3) Commission timing: payouts after Redwood receives funds (net collections). For reseller margin, we will issue monthly statements and pay the following net 30. For referral one-time credits, payable within 45 days of invoice.

4) Clawback: 12-month clawback on refunds/chargebacks tied to referred deals. Clawback method spelled out in appendix.

5) Legal redlines: attached quick markups in Drive (see link). If Beacon is comfortable, we can prepare a DocuSign MoU for signatures after procurement review.

Drive redlines: https://drive.redwood-inference.com/drive/folders/partnerships/beacon
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.example/record/HS-789234

I can join Friday's call to run through operational flow and sign-off checklist.

— Karthik

Thanks everyone — good alignment across commercial and ops. Quick summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

- Redwood + Beacon agree to default 90-day registration protection; enterprise exceptions (> $250k ARR) extend to 12 months after joint qualification.
- Commission structure: referral credit (8% one-time on first-year net ARR) OR reseller margin (18% first year / 10% renewals). Implementation fee split 60/40 when Beacon delivers services.
- Payouts: monthly statements; payments after net collections (referral credits within 45 days; reseller margin net 30). 12-month clawback applies.
- Escrow: start with HubSpot + archived confirmation email as canonical record. If Beacon requires third-party custody, we'll iterate in contract appendix.
- Action items: 
  1) Beacon procurement/legal to review MoU (Evelyn: sent Beacon_MoU_draft_v2.pdf).
  2) Karthik to incorporate the 90/12 month registration language and payout timelines in a redlined MoU.
  3) Ben/Camila to finalize commission workbook and share final tabulated examples.
  4) Schedule DocuSign execution once both legal teams clear.

Proposed call to finalize: Friday Aug 20, 10:00 PT — please confirm availability.

Evelyn
